reconcile.note: Gill answers that John's silence about the kiss is simply an omission of a detail the other evangelists already recorded, not a denial that it happened.

discrepancy.note: Strauss treats the Judas-kiss versus John's self-identification as one instance of the Synoptic-vs-John divergence in the arrest scene's mechanics.

quotes.text: According to the three first Evangelists, Judas steps forth and kisses Jesus, in order by this preconcerted sign to indicate him to the approaching band as the individual whom they were to seize: according to the fourth gospel, on the contrary, Jesus advances apparently out of the garden ( ἐξελθὼν ) to meet them, and presents himself as the person whom they seek.
quotes.attr: David Friedrich Strauss (d. 1874), The Life of Jesus Critically Examined (1846), on the Synoptic-vs-John divergence in the mechanics of Jesus's arrest.

sides.snippet: Whoever I kiss, he is the one. Seize him.
sides.verseText: Now he who betrayed him gave them a sign, saying, \"Whoever I kiss, he is the one. Seize him.\"

sides.snippet: Jesus said to them, \"I AM.\" Judas also, who betrayed him, was standing with them.
sides.verseText: They answered him, \"Jesus of Nazareth.\" Jesus said to them, \"I AM.\" Judas also, who betrayed him, was standing with them.
